# Path

A borrowed path.

```rux
pub struct Path {
    pub name: OsStringView;
}
```

`Copy`, owning nothing: structure over an [`OsStringView`](/docs/api/path/os-string-view)'s units.

## Methods

<h3 id="parent"><code>Parent</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Parent(self: &Path) -> Path?
```

This path without its last component, or `none` where nothing is left to remove.
The parent of `/a` is `/`, and the root's parent is `none`: the root is not inside anything. The parent of
a bare segment is the empty path, which is what lets a loop walk parents to a fixed end.

**Returns**: the path without its last component, or `none` when there is none to remove

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Path/Src/Path.rux#L15)

<h3 id="file-name"><code>FileName</code></h3>

```rux
pub func FileName(self: &Path) -> OsStringView?
```

The last component's name, or `none` for the empty path and the root.
Trailing separators are ignored: `a/b/` names `b`, because that is what everything from shells to
libraries has always meant by it.

**Returns**: the last component, or `none` for a root or a path ending in a separator

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Path/Src/Path.rux#L40)

<h3 id="stem"><code>Stem</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Stem(self: &Path) -> OsStringView?
```

The file name before its extension, or `none` where there is no file name.
A leading dot is part of the name, not an extension marker: the stem of `.bashrc` is `.bashrc`. Of
`a.tar.gz` it is `a.tar` — one extension comes off, the last.

**Returns**: the file name without its extension, or `none` when there is no file name

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Path/Src/Path.rux#L60)

<h3 id="extension"><code>Extension</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Extension(self: &Path) -> OsStringView?
```

The extension after the last dot, without the dot, or `none` where there is none.
`none` for `.bashrc` and for `Makefile` alike: a name that is all extension has none.

**Returns**: the file name's extension without the dot, or `none` when it has none

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Path/Src/Path.rux#L74)

<h3 id="equals"><code>Equals</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Equals(self: &Path, other: Path) -> bool
```

Whether two paths are the same units.
Lexical, not semantic: `a/b` and `a//b` name the same file and are different paths here. Making them equal
is normalization's job, asked for by name.

| Name    | Type   | Description                  |
| ------- | ------ | ---------------------------- |
| `other` | `Path` | the value to compare against |

**Returns**: whether both hold the same units in the same order, without normalizing either

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Path/Src/Path.rux#L89)

## Implements Display

`Path` conforms to `Display`.

<h3 id="write-display"><code>WriteDisplay</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteDisplay(
    self: &Path,
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec
) -> ! FormatError
```

The lossy rendering of the path's units.
The separators are written as they stand: a path is shown as it is, not normalized towards the platform's
preferred separator, because which separators a name contains is part of what it is.
The failures [`OsStringView::WriteDisplay`](/docs/api/path/os-string-view#write-display) reports.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the whole path was accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Path/Src/Path.rux#L267)

## Related

<h3 id="component-iterator"><code>ComponentIterator</code></h3>

```rux
pub struct ComponentIterator {
    // private fields
}
```

A walk over a path's segments.
Runs of separators count as one, and a trailing separator ends the walk rather than yielding an empty segment:
`a//b/` walks as `a`, `b`. A leading separator is the root, which the walk reports as an empty first component
so that an absolute path is distinguishable from a relative one holding the same segments.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Path/Src/Path.rux#L107)
